Limit how often an asynchronous function can be called

Source: R/async_rate_limit.R
async_rate_limit.Rd

Asynchronous version of rate_limit(). It allows at most calls calls to start in any window of period seconds, but a call over the limit is scheduled with later::later() instead of sleeping, so the session carries on. The decorated function returns a promise that follows the wrapped function's result, a plain value or a promise.

Usage

async_rate_limit(f, calls, period = 1)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

calls

Maximum number of calls in one window. A whole number of at least 1.

period

Length of the window in seconds. Defaults to 1.

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns a promise.

Details

Each call reserves its slot when it is made, so calls start in order and queued calls count toward the limit. As with rate_limit(), an error still uses its slot. It limits when calls start, not how many run, so slow calls can overlap. Stack it inside async_retry() to throttle every attempt.

Needs the promises and later packages, and an event loop.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f := async_rate_limit(calls = 2, period = 0.2) %@% function(i) i
start <- Sys.time()
for (i in 1:4) {
  local({
    i <- i
    promises::then(f(i), function(value) {
      cat("call", value, "at", round(as.numeric(Sys.time() - start), 1), "s\n")
    })
  })
}
while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.05)
} # }
